title: Research: price the paid-mass elimination budget of the selected complex word (screening budget; no new kappa)
body:
## Summary

Prices the paid-mass axis of the selected complex word's packing relaxation, as an exact screening budget for decoder and helper-inventory proposals (card `complex-new-helper-inventory`, scope **refined**, priority revision 6). No new κ; the selected record is unchanged.

```text
inherited ceiling (nothing removed)      0.001690054109089
whole-child curve, seven breakpoints     0.003081073334575 -> 0.013675160009708
bit primitive budget 0.00173343 needs     phi >= 2.3948528 %   (133.78 of 5586 mass units/call)
1/99 planning target needs                phi >= 92.7698485 %  (5182.12 of 5586)
full elimination is                      8.0916x the inherited ceiling, 1.354x the 1/99 target
```

The inherited relaxation holds the selected per-call paid profile `{1:2412, 2:418, 3:432, 4:142, 5:82, 8:8}` fixed. This package adds one axis: a proposal removes paid mass, the removed mass stays inside the coverage budget and is re-packed as ideal rank-51 idle children, and removal is free. The optimal removal takes the lowest-rank paid children first, because the per-unit saving `r^-a m^(a-1) - R^-a m^(a-1)` is strictly decreasing in `r`. So a proposal that removes less than `2.3949 %` cannot make the bit side bind under the retained balanced reduction, whatever else it does, and no change confined to this word's mass distribution reaches the 1/99 planning target unless it removes `92.77 %` of paid mass at zero realization cost.

This is a favorable relaxation and a screen, not a construction: real removal pays something, so a physical proposal must remove more than these thresholds.

## Evidence

Exact 256-bit rational enclosures from the pinned predecessor module `research/complex-local-word-ceiling/ceiling.py`, imported unchanged as a live input. `verify.py` reproduces the predecessor ceiling at φ=0, certifies the seven whole-child breakpoints (strictly increasing, bracket width < 1e-15), certifies the three φ thresholds (bisection tolerance 1e-9 mass units), checks the lowest-rank-first optimality ordering at four exponents with a rank-reversed rejection control, checks full elimination against the closed-form pure-idle moment at three exponents, and rejects a target above the full-elimination ceiling. Nine controls rejected; `PASS_COMPLEX_PAID_MASS_BUDGET`.

The card's first working example is the inherited positive control: `python3 -B research/complex-local-word-ceiling/verify.py` prints `PASS_COMPLEX_LOCAL_WORD_CEILING a_ceiling 0.00169005410908900006`.

Reproduction (from a repository root, CPython 3.12 at `~/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12`, standard library only):

```sh
python3 -I -B research/complex-paid-mass-budget/verify.py            # ~17 s
python3 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/complex-paid-mass-budget
python3 -B scripts/check_research_commit.py --package research/complex-paid-mass-budget --check-source-history
```

Local results: `PASS_REGISTERED_RESEARCH_PACKAGE ... outcome=partial` and `PASS_RESEARCH_COMMIT_BYTES` at commit `f8160fe2866d05be048d8297c5ab64a806617b94`, base `20ecf2891d80b5acf18d980b2164fb44ea7faa90`. CI replay is the authoritative environment for the registered command; local wall time is about 17 s, well inside the 10-minute limit.

## Scope and what is not claimed

- Favorable relaxation: removal is free and fractional children are allowed; whole-child breakpoints are reported separately for physical reading.
- Fixed to the selected word, 112 ports, the nine-stage four-pair template, one unpaid coordinate per live family, centre charge 64 and the guard `R = 51`.
- Not a supplier, not a κ, not a certificate and not a selected-frontier change. Not a complete multiplication theorem.
- At the selected endpoint φ = 0, so this budget does not measure the selected construction's own slack.

## Credit

The coverage identity is PR1012's. The packing ceiling, its exact arithmetic and the lever table are Douglas Colkitt's `complex-local-word-ceiling` package, imported unchanged. Prepared by Nick Petalas with AI assistance; independent human and formal proof-kernel review are unclaimed.
